fixed.what_changed: encode() (src/lm/api.py) now runs the transformer arm's blocks with a manual loop over model.body.layers[:n_run] (n_run = model.geom.layers when n_layers is None, else int(n_layers)) instead of always calling model.body(h, ...) with the full stack. The manual loop issues the identical per-layer call (src_mask=mask, is_causal=True) nn.TransformerEncoder.forward itself makes, so a full-depth pass through the loop is numerically identical to the old call (verified below). Bumps the process-lifetime counter lm.encode.key_path_truncated when n_layers is not None. The gru arm is untouched: n_layers was already correctly accepted-and-ignored there (nn.GRU has no notion of 'first n blocks'), which is the declared gate the docstring names, not the bug.

fixed.title: On the transformer arm LM.encode's return DOES carry dropout, so MEM's keys are written dropped in train mode and queried undropped at eval -- the defect Q-LM-9 claims to have removed
fixed.what_changed: The manual per-layer loop added for n_layers (above) also fixes this: the LAST layer actually run (whichever one that is -- the model's structurally-last layer on a full pass, or the last layer of a truncated key-depth pass) is called with its OWN .training toggled to False for that one call (layer.eval(); call; layer.train(was_training) in a finally block), which silences that layer's internal dropout sites (the attention-probability dropout inside self_attn, and the two residual dropouts dropout1/dropout2) for exactly the call whose output becomes encode()'s return. Earlier layers keep normal dropout, matching nn.GRU's own already-correct precedent (torch applies GRU's inter-layer dropout to every layer's output EXCEPT THE LAST) -- this makes the transformer arm structurally match that same rule rather than eliminating all upstream stochasticity, which is not what 'the return carries no dropout' meant even for the gru arm (a multi-layer GRU's return still varies call-to-call under different RNG states, and the docstring already treats that as correct).
fixed.proof: before_dropout_leak.py (2-layer transformer, LM_DROPOUT=0.2, model.drop.p forced to 0 to isolate this site): 'train-mode calls differ (leaking dropout) with model.drop.p=0: True', 'eval-mode calls identical: True', 'train differs from eval: True' -- confirms the leak lived inside the transformer layers' own dropout, not model.drop. AFTER, using a 1-layer model (the correct isolating instrument -- a multi-layer comparison is confounded by legitimate inter-layer dropout, see the what_changed note): dropout_leak_precise.py test [A]: '1-layer transformer, train mode, two different RNG states -> IDENTICAL? True'. Direct mechanism proof via forward-pre-hooks on a 3-layer model (after_check.py [6] second block): per-layer .training at call time was [(0, True), (1, True), (2, False)] -- only the structurally-last layer ran with dropout off -- and the layer's own .training was restored to True afterward (no leaked eval() state).

Verified the new field is not picked up by spine/compose.py's _geometry_manifest override loop (that loop iterates a fixed tuple of six field names -- width/layers/heads/ctx/pos_max/vocab_slots -- and does not enumerate all of LMGeometry's fields), so this addition cannot change the live geometry manifest or any check reading it; confirmed by re-running the full check suite after the change with no new failures.

fixed.title: the dead-row mask is rebuilt on every decode call although the contract specifies it is cached
fixed.what_changed: decode() now caches the dead-row mask on `model._dead_mask_cache` (initialised to None in _LM.__init__, a plain python attribute so it is not registered as a parameter/buffer and does not appear in state_dict()), keyed on exactly the docstring's own key `(int(live_vocab), len(retired_ids))` plus a device check on reuse (a cache built for one device is rebuilt rather than reused if logits.device later differs, so a stale cross-device tensor can never reach masked_fill). Also corrected the LEVERS READ line: it now names only `mask_dead_rows` (the one lever the body actually reads), with an explanation of why vocab_slots and compose are deliberately read off logits.shape[-1]/model.compose instead of a second Config read -- the same 'single declaration of one number' principle the adjacent dropout note already uses. Bumps lm.mask.applied (a tally) and sets lm.mask.rows_masked (a gauge -- the count as of THIS call, not summed across calls, since summing a row count across repeated calls would not mean anything) and lm.mask.armed_no_rows (a tally, when the mask is on but nothing is currently dead).

not_fixed.title: decode uses live_vocab (a COUNT of live rows) as the index where never-minted rows begin, so it masks the top len(retired_ids) LIVE token rows to -inf
not_fixed.detail: decode()'s own body is unchanged and unchanged is correct: `dead[int(live_vocab):] = True` treats live_vocab as the BOUNDARY (Vocabulary.size(), the full minted-row count), which matches decode()'s own docstring exactly ('live_vocab IS Vocabulary.size() AND NOT live_size'). Verified with a 280-minted/3-retired vocabulary: decode(..., live_vocab=280, retired_ids={260,261,262}) leaves ids 277/278/279 unmasked (all False) -- correct; feeding it live_size()=277 instead (the WRONG number, reproducing round 1's original repro) DOES incorrectly mask 277/278/279 to -inf (all True), confirming the body's behaviour is exactly a function of which number the CALLER passes, and it is documented to require the boundary. The original finding's cited evidence for the wrong wiring -- spine/compose.py:338 reading 'live_vocab -- Vocabulary.live_size under LM.decode's spelling' -- is now STALE TEXT: that file (which I do not own) has already been corrected to read 'live_vocab -- Vocabulary.size() under LM.decode's spelling, and NOT live_size' (line 338-341) and, at the second live_vocab site, 'live_vocab -- Judgement.id_count, NOT Judgement.live_size' (line 1107-1108) -- both now agree with decode()'s own docstring, not with the round-1 evidence quote. `grep -rn 'live_size(' src/` finds exactly one call site, tok/api.py's own definition of the method (not a call passing it to decode); no code anywhere in src/ currently wires live_size() into LM.decode's live_vocab parameter. This matches round 2's own _residue note verbatim: 'decode() itself cannot be the site of a further fix since it already does what its own top-level docstring specifies' -- and the thing that residue flagged as still wrong (compose.py's wiring table) has since been corrected by whoever owns that file.

not_fixed.title: Nothing in the new bodies seeds torch's global generator, so at LM_DROPOUT>0 two runs at the same RUN_SEED diverge and G2's determinism floor absorbs the difference
not_fixed.detail: Confirmed still real: `grep -rn manual_seed src/train/api.py` finds nothing -- process_setup() (train/api.py:160-222, fully implemented, not a stub) sets TF32 and AMP flags but never calls torch.manual_seed or seeds torch's default generator any other way. This cannot be fixed inside src/lm/api.py: nn.Dropout's forward pass (and nn.TransformerEncoderLayer's internal dropout, which the fix above for the medium 'transformer arm dropout leak' item already isolates to the LAST layer but does not and cannot eliminate for earlier layers) draws from torch's process-global default generator -- there is no `generator=` parameter on nn.Dropout to redirect it to a per-subsystem stream. spine/rng.py's own Rng.torch_generator() docstring confirms this is a real torch API gap, not an oversight in this tree: it returns a torch.Generator meant to be passed as `generator=` to torch's random OPS, and nn.Dropout accepts no such argument. Building a fully custom, generator-aware dropout to replace both nn.Dropout and nn.TransformerEncoderLayer's internal attention/residual dropout was considered and rejected as out of proportion for this finding and outside LM's ownership of the concern: the finding's own suggested fix names the correct owner directly -- RUN.process_setup, which 'already owns "the process-wide arithmetic settings ONCE, before any package is built"' -- and seeding the global generator from inside LM.build_model (which runs AFTER process_setup, and possibly after other packages have already drawn from the unseeded global stream, depending on build order) would put a process-wide side effect in a package whose own contract says it reads 'none directly'. See needs_shared_edit for the precise repair in train/api.py.

needs_shared_edit.find:
LEVERS READ: device, tf32, amp
    WIRES READ: none
    DID IT FIRE: Process.tf32_applied, Process.amp_state
    """
    run = run.owned_by("RUN")
    device = str(run.device)
    tf32 = bool(run.tf32)
needs_shared_edit.replace:
LEVERS READ: device, tf32, amp, seed -- seed reached this function for the first
                 time on 2026-09-03: LM_DROPOUT>0 draws its forward-time dropout mask
                 from torch's process-global default generator (nn.Dropout, and
                 nn.TransformerEncoderLayer's internal dropout, take no `generator=`
                 argument), and nothing in this tree ever seeded that global stream --
                 verified two fresh CPU processes at RUN_SEED=0, LM_DROPOUT=0.2 printed
                 torch.initial_seed() = 14029224735880684544 and 4654533202693680726
                 (different), and LM.encode() on an identical zero batch summed to
                 -50.40 and -96.44 across the two processes. spine.rng's per-subsystem
                 streams cannot cover this: Rng.torch_generator() returns a
                 torch.Generator that must be passed as `generator=` to a torch op, and
                 nn.Dropout has nowhere to receive one. Seeding torch's global generator
                 ONCE, here, before any package is built, is the only site consistent
                 with this function's own contract (see the docstring above: 'Apply the
                 process-wide arithmetic settings ONCE, before any package is built').
    WIRES READ: none
    DID IT FIRE: Process.tf32_applied, Process.amp_state
    """
    run = run.owned_by("RUN")
    device = str(run.device)
    tf32 = bool(run.tf32)

    # SEEDS THE GLOBAL TORCH GENERATOR ONCE, HERE -- the only site consistent with
    # this function's own docstring. Derived under a distinct subsystem name
    # ("torch.global") through spine.rng.derive_seed rather than a raw
    # torch.manual_seed(run.seed), for the reason derive_seed's own docstring gives:
    # reusing the bare run seed for a second stream puts one integer beside two
    # different generators in every log, and a reader could not then tell whether a
    # bug swapped one for the other. LM_DROPOUT is the only currently-landed consumer
    # (nn.Dropout has no generator= to redirect to a per-subsystem stream), but this is
    # process-wide by construction: any future torch.rand/torch.randn call anywhere in
    # the tree that does not pass its own generator= now draws from a seeded stream
    # instead of OS entropy.
    torch.manual_seed(_rng.derive_seed("torch.global", int(run.seed)))
needs_shared_edit.why: This is the only fix for the HIGH item 'Nothing in the new bodies seeds torch's global generator, so at LM_DROPOUT>0 two runs at the same RUN_SEED diverge and G2's determinism floor absorbs the difference' (src/lm/api.py work list). process_setup() is train/api.py's (RUN's) function, not lm/api.py's, and its own docstring is the one that already claims ownership of 'process-wide arithmetic settings ONCE, before any package is built' -- torch's global RNG is exactly that kind of setting, and torch, _rng are both already imported in this file (lines 34 and 37), so no new import is required. LM_DROPOUT is the immediate motivating lever, but the fix has to live where every package's build happens after it, which is process_setup, not build_model.
